claims.text: Replacing the conventional Cu matrix with a Cu-Cr-Zr alloy matrix will increase the thermal conductivity of the W-Cu composite.
The thermal-conductivity increase will be 25-40% relative to an otherwise comparable conventional W-Cu composite.
A Cu-Cr-Zr matrix has a lower density of defects that scatter phonons than a conventional Cu matrix.
A Cu-Cr-Zr matrix has fewer phonon-scattering impurities than a conventional Cu matrix.
Reducing the density of defects and impurities that scatter phonons increases the composite's thermal conductivity.
Replacing the Cu matrix with a Cu-Cr-Zr matrix will retain or significantly improve the mechanical durability of the W-Cu composite.
The Cu-Cr-Zr matrix has higher strength than the conventional Cu matrix.
The higher strength of the Cu-Cr-Zr matrix improves the mechanical durability of the composite.
Replacing the Cu matrix with a Cu-Cr-Zr matrix will retain or significantly improve the irradiation resistance of the W-Cu composite.
The Cu-Cr-Zr matrix is more resistant to radiation-induced damage than a conventional Cu matrix.
The proposed performance gains should hold at operating temperatures of 500-1000°C.
The proposed performance gains should hold under neutron irradiation doses of 1-10 dpa.
The magnitude of the thermal, mechanical, and irradiation-resistance changes may depend on the specific Cu-Cr-Zr composition and processing.
The proposed test compares conventional-Cu-matrix and Cu-Cr-Zr-matrix W-Cu composites under the same operating conditions.
